title: Ripple launch-update result
description: Output of the Bayesian update: prior = the fitted posterior, likelihood = the observed launch weeks, result = importance-weighted posterior. Produced by web/lib/update.ts (browser, ESS gate) and model/ripple_model/update.py (reference, PSIS gate); the parity test asserts both agree on the weighted summaries.

weeks_used.description: Position of the week slider. 0 = no real data yet, so the result equals the prior forecast.

gate.description: Validity of the fast update. When ok is false the UI shows 'Refit needed' and the API refits the full model.

criterion.description: 'ess' in the browser (weight effective sample size, needs >= 300); 'pareto_k' in Python (PSIS k-hat, needs <= 0.7).

ess.description: Effective sample size of the importance weights, always reported.

pareto_k.description: PSIS k-hat; null in the browser, which does not smooth the weights.

smoothed.description: True when the weights were Pareto-smoothed (Python only).

message.description: Plain-English badge text, e.g. 'Fast update reliable (ESS 1,840 of 20,000)'.

unknown.description: What the launch taught us about the one unknown. Drives the prior-vs-posterior density plot.

prior_percent.description: Same prior as a percent lift, when display is percent_lift — so the UI never converts a number itself.

density.description: Shared grid for the small prior-vs-posterior plot.

forecast.description: Updated forecast over the launch horizon, using the importance-weighted draws.

total_profit.description: Gross profit of all launch cells over the horizon, minus fixed_cost. NOT a verdict for an offer or feature launch, where these cells are an existing business.

incremental_profit.description: THE HEADLINE. (mu_forecast - mu_counterfactual) x (price - unit_cost), summed over the horizon, minus fixed_cost, differenced inside each sample before any summary. Equals total_profit for a new city, whose counterfactual is zero.

p_profit_positive.description: Share of weight on samples with incremental_profit > 0 — the 'chance it pays' number.

units.description: Updated predictive band for this week.

observed_units.description: The real point, when this week is inside weeks_used; null for future weeks.

counterfactual_units.description: What the model expects with NO change — the baseline the lift is measured against.

prior_forecast.description: The same forecast before any launch data, so the UI can show 'Chance it pays: 61% → 78%'.

mode.description: 'experiment' when the data has a randomized holdout column; otherwise 'model_based' (observed vs. the model's counterfactual).

label.description: Badge text, e.g. 'Model-based estimate' or 'Experiment (random holdout)'.

recommendation.description: e.g. 'Keep a random 10% holdout next time — then this is an experiment, not an estimate.'

n_prior_draws.description: D posterior draws reused as the prior, e.g. 1000.

k_per_draw.description: K values of the unknown drawn per posterior draw, e.g. 20.

n_samples.description: D * K joint prior samples, e.g. 20000.

n_obs_cells.description: Observed rows that entered the likelihood.

prior_sigma.description: Scale actually used for a skeptical feature prior.
